newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot drops plans for GE engines on Il-86 jets.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot drops plans for GE engines on Il-86 jets.

text.p: Russia's international carrier Aeroflot has abandoned plans to modernise its wide-body Ilyushin Il-86 jets with CFM-56 engines from General Electric and Snecma, the airline said on Friday.

"This project is not efficient and...Aeroflot will drop out of it," said an Aeroflot statement. GE signed a memorandum of understanding in 1995 to modernise 18 Aeroflot Il-86s at a cost of $30 million for each of the four-engined, 350-seat planes.

Russian airlines Pulkovo, KrasAir and Sibavia also said at the time they were considering fitting the GE engines to their Russian-built Il-86 aircraft, while Kazakhstan Airways also said it planned to modernise its Il-86 fleet.
The Aeroflot announcement does not affect plans for a new Il-96 jet fitted with Pratt & Whitney engines. U.S. Pratt & Whitney is a division of United Technologies Corp.
A GE official in Moscow said he had no information about the Aeroflot decision. "I am hearing about it for the first time," he said.
